線性代數、機率統計與 Python 各自在圖形識別中的角色
The role each of linear algebra, probability/statistics, and Python plays in pattern recognition

PR115 圖形識別 · §1 課程說明與導論 · KP-02

這三樣不是入場券，不是「有沒有」的問題，而是「熟不熟」的問題。
These three aren't an admission ticket — the question isn't "do you have them," it's "how comfortable are you with them."

情境引入 | Scenario

🧑‍🎓
研究生：「老師，大綱寫先備知識要線性代數……我大二線代只有 62 分，我是不是死定了？」
"Professor, the syllabus says linear algebra is a prerequisite... I only got 62 in sophomore linear algebra. Am I doomed?"
👨‍🏫
教授：「我先問你：你當年學線代的時候，有人告訴你那些東西要拿來幹嘛嗎？」
"Let me ask you first: back when you learned linear algebra, did anyone tell you what any of it was actually for?"
🧑‍🎓
研究生：「……沒有。就是一直算行列式。」
"...No. It was just computing determinants over and over."
👨‍🏫
教授：「那就對了。這門課會把每一個工具放回它該在的位置。你會發現你不是不會，是沒被告訴要用在哪。」
"Exactly. This course puts every tool back where it belongs. You'll find you weren't incapable — you just were never told where to use it."

1三根柱子 | Three Pillars

🏛️ 圖 1：三根柱子撐起圖形識別 | Fig. 1: Three pillars holding up pattern recognition

線性代數 | Linear Algebra

負責「空間」——東西擺在哪、離多遠、往哪個方向看比較清楚。
In charge of "space" — where things sit, how far apart, and which direction gives the clearest view.

機率統計 | Probability & Statistics

負責「不確定」——不敢肯定時，怎麼把「大概」變成可計算的數字。
In charge of "uncertainty" — turning a vague "probably" into a number you can compute with, when you can't be sure.

Python

負責「動手」——把前兩者從紙上搬到螢幕，親眼確認它們沒騙你。
In charge of "doing it" — moving the other two from paper onto the screen so you can see with your own eyes that they weren't lying.

2線性代數只在講「怎麼看東西」| What Linear Algebra Really Does

1
向量 = 一個物件的資料卡 | Vector = An Object's Data Card

$x=(4.6,\ 1.12)$ 不是抽象的「有方向的量」，就是一張填好的表格。
$x=(4.6, 1.12)$ isn't some abstract "quantity with direction" — it's just a filled-in form.

2
內積 = 相似度與投影 | Dot Product = Similarity and Projection

$w^{\top}x$ 有兩個身分：算總分（權重×特徵）與量相似（單位向量時 $w^{\top}x=\cos\theta$）。第二個身分正是 §8 樣板匹配的核心。
$w^{\top}x$ wears two hats: computing a total score (weight × feature) and measuring similarity (for unit vectors, $w^{\top}x=\cos\theta$). The second hat is the heart of §8's template matching.

3
特徵值／特徵向量 = 資料的主軸 | Eigenvalues/Eigenvectors = The Data's Main Axis

資料像一根斜斜的雪茄：特徵向量說長軸朝哪，特徵值說那個方向有多長。這就是 §6 的 PCA。
Data looks like a tilted cigar: the eigenvector says which way the long axis points, the eigenvalue says how long it is in that direction. That's §6's PCA.

4
矩陣 = 一次搬動一整組資料 | Matrix = Moving a Whole Batch at Once

要對一萬筆資料做同一件事，不寫一萬次乘法——寫一次矩陣乘法。矩陣是批次處理的縮寫。
To do the same thing to ten thousand data points, you don't write ten thousand multiplications — you write one matrix multiplication. A matrix is shorthand for batch processing.

3看一次投影就懂 §6 的一半 | Projection in Action

📉 圖 2：80 個二維點沿主方向投影成一維（實際計算） | Fig. 2: 80 two-dimensional points projected onto the principal direction, down to one dimension (real computation)
主方向 $u=(0.82,\ 0.57)$。用一個數字取代兩個數字，卻仍保留 96.7% 的變異——這就是降維划算在哪裡。
Principal direction $u=(0.82, 0.57)$. Replace two numbers with one, yet keep 96.7% of the variance — that's exactly where dimensionality reduction pays off.

4為什麼非用機率不可？| Why Probability Is Unavoidable

因為真實資料重疊。不是所有小型動物都是貓——還有吉娃娃。
既然錯誤無法避免，就別假裝可以避免：改成計算「最少會錯多少」，再證明你的方法達到了那個下限。
Because real data overlaps. Not every small animal is a cat — there are also chihuahuas. Since errors can't be avoided, stop pretending they can: instead compute "the minimum unavoidable error rate," then prove your method reaches that floor.
📊 圖 3：重疊、最佳門檻與躲不掉的誤差 | Fig. 3: Overlap, the optimal threshold, and the unavoidable error

交點 $x^{*}=6.09$ 是最佳門檻；紅色陰影是無論多聰明都躲不掉的錯誤，此例約 8.15%。這就是 §2 貝氏決策理論的靈魂。
The crossing point $x^{*}=6.09$ is the optimal threshold; the red shaded area is the error no amount of cleverness can avoid — about 8.15% here. This is the soul of §2's Bayesian decision theory.

5四個關鍵詞的白話版 | Four Words, Plain Language

術語 | Term符號 | Symbol白話 | Plain Language
先驗機率 | Prior$P(\omega_i)$還沒看資料之前，你原本覺得它是哪一類的機會
How likely you thought each class was, before seeing any data
概似 | Likelihood$p(x\mid\omega_i)$如果它真的是第 $i$ 類，長成 $x$ 這樣有多合理
If it really were class $i$, how plausible is it to look like $x$
後驗機率 | Posterior$P(\omega_i\mid x)$看完資料之後，你更新過的想法
Your updated belief after seeing the data
期望值 | Expectation$E[\cdot]$如果這樣做一萬次，平均要付出多少代價
If you did this ten thousand times, what's the average cost
$$P(\omega_i \mid x) = \frac{p(x\mid\omega_i)\,P(\omega_i)}{p(x)}$$

白話翻譯：新的想法 = 原本的想法 × 證據的支持度，再除以一個讓機率加總為 1 的常數。
它就是「看到證據要改想法」這件常識的數學版。
Plain-language translation: new belief = old belief × how much the evidence supports it, divided by a constant that makes the probabilities sum to 1. It's the math version of the common-sense rule "update your beliefs when you see evidence."

6動手算一次 | A Worked Example

設定：$P(\omega_1)=0.6,\ \mu_1=4.5,\ \sigma_1=1.0$；$P(\omega_2)=0.4,\ \mu_2=7.5,\ \sigma_2=1.2$。觀測到 $x=6.0$，它是哪一類？
Setup: $P(\omega_1)=0.6, \mu_1=4.5, \sigma_1=1.0$; $P(\omega_2)=0.4, \mu_2=7.5, \sigma_2=1.2$. We observe $x=6.0$ — which class is it?

Step 1　算概似 | Compute the Likelihoods

$$p(6.0\mid\omega_1)=\tfrac{1}{1.0\sqrt{2\pi}}e^{-\frac{(6.0-4.5)^2}{2}}=0.3989\times0.3247=0.1295$$ $$p(6.0\mid\omega_2)=\tfrac{1}{1.2\sqrt{2\pi}}e^{-\frac{(6.0-7.5)^2}{2(1.44)}}=0.3324\times0.4578=0.1522$$

Step 2　乘上先驗 | Multiply by the Priors

$$\omega_1:\ 0.1295\times0.6=0.0777 \qquad \omega_2:\ 0.1522\times0.4=0.0609$$

$0.0777 > 0.0609$ ⟹ 判給 $\omega_1$

微妙之處：光看概似，$\omega_2$ 其實比較高（0.1522 > 0.1295）！但因為第一類本來就比較常見，最後仍判給第一類。
這就是先驗的力量——在機率的世界裡，成見是有正當地位的。
Here's the subtlety: by likelihood alone, $\omega_2$ is actually higher (0.1522 > 0.1295)! But because class 1 is simply more common, it still wins in the end. This is the power of the prior — in the world of probability, preconceptions have a legitimate place.

7Python：把數學從紙上救出來 | Verify It Yourself

🐍 Python — 四行核心邏輯跑完 §2 的決策規則 | Four lines of core logic running §2's decision rule
import numpy as np

def gauss(x, mu, sigma):
    """一維常態機率密度 p(x) = 1/(sigma*sqrt(2pi)) * exp(-(x-mu)^2 / (2 sigma^2))"""
    return np.exp(-0.5 * ((x - mu) / sigma) ** 2) / (sigma * np.sqrt(2 * np.pi))

x = 6.0
prior = {"w1": 0.6, "w2": 0.4}                  # 先驗機率 P(omega_i)
like  = {"w1": gauss(x, 4.5, 1.0),              # 概似 p(x | omega_i)
         "w2": gauss(x, 7.5, 1.2)}

# 後驗的分子：P(omega_i) * p(x | omega_i)；分母 p(x) 對兩類相同，比大小可省略
score = {k: prior[k] * like[k] for k in prior}
print(like)                                      # {'w1': 0.1295, 'w2': 0.1522}
print(score)                                     # {'w1': 0.0777, 'w2': 0.0609}
print("判給:", max(score, key=score.get))        # 判給: w1
✅
驗證理解最快的方式是跑一遍：那個 0.0777 對不對？三行就知道。
The fastest way to check your understanding is to run it: is that 0.0777 correct? Three lines will tell you.
✅
NumPy 就是線性代數的手：$w^{\top}x$ 寫作 w @ x，特徵分解寫作 np.linalg.eigh(C)。
NumPy is linear algebra's hands: $w^{\top}x$ becomes w @ x, eigendecomposition becomes np.linalg.eigh(C).
✅
畫圖是最強的除錯工具：分類器效果不好，先把資料畫出來看一眼。
Plotting is the strongest debugging tool: if a classifier performs poorly, plot the data and look at it first.
✅
期末專案硬性要求 Git + AI 智能體協作，你得讀得懂並改得動 AI 的產出。
The final project mandates Git + AI-agent collaboration — you must be able to read and modify what the AI produces.

8誠實的自我檢核清單 | Honest Self-Check

不是要你全部會，是要你知道自己哪裡不會。
The goal isn't for you to know everything — it's for you to know exactly where you don't.

線性代數 · 4 項 | Linear Algebra · 4 Items▼
  • 我知道 $w^{\top}x$ 怎麼算，也知道它可以表示「相似度」
    I know how to compute $w^{\top}x$, and that it can represent "similarity"
  • 我知道矩陣乘向量代表「對這個向量做一次線性變換」
    I know that matrix times vector means "applying a linear transformation to that vector"
  • 我看到「特徵值分解」不會腦袋一片空白，知道它在找資料的主軸
    "Eigendecomposition" doesn't make my mind go blank — I know it's finding the data's principal axes
  • 我知道「向量投影到某方向」在幾何上是什麼意思
    I know what "projecting a vector onto a direction" means geometrically
機率統計 · 4 項 | Probability & Statistics · 4 Items▼
  • 我能區分 $P(A\mid B)$ 和 $P(B\mid A)$ 不一樣（最常見的錯誤）
    I can tell $P(A\mid B)$ and $P(B\mid A)$ apart — the most common mistake
  • 我看得懂常態分布的公式，知道 $\mu$ 和 $\sigma$ 各控制什麼
    I can read the normal-distribution formula and know what $\mu$ and $\sigma$ each control
  • 我知道「期望值」是加權平均
    I know "expectation" is a weighted average
  • 我聽過貝氏定理，即使還不會用
    I've heard of Bayes' theorem, even if I can't use it yet
Python · 3 項 | Python · 3 Items▼
  • 我能用 NumPy 建立陣列、做矩陣乘法
    I can create arrays and do matrix multiplication with NumPy
  • 我能用 matplotlib 畫散佈圖
    I can draw a scatter plot with matplotlib
  • 我會用 Git 做 commit（期末專案硬性要求）
    I can make a Git commit (a hard requirement for the final project)
打勾不到一半也沒關係——但請把沒打勾的項目寫下來。
準備清單第 2 條的用字是「標出不熟的部分」，不是「補完」。
It's fine if you check off less than half — but write down the items you didn't check. Item 2 of the prep list says "mark" the unfamiliar parts, not "finish" them.

知識檢定 | Knowledge Check

1
數值計算 | Numerical Calculation
承正文設定，若觀測到 $x=7.0$，請重算兩類的 $P(\omega_i)p(x\mid\omega_i)$ 並判斷類別。
Using the same setup, if we observe $x=7.0$, recompute $P(\omega_i)p(x\mid\omega_i)$ for both classes and determine the class.
✅ 正確答案：
$p(7.0\mid\omega_1)=0.3989\,e^{-\frac{(2.5)^2}{2}}=0.3989\times0.0439=0.0175$；乘先驗 $\times0.6=0.0105$。
$p(7.0\mid\omega_2)=0.3324\,e^{-\frac{(0.5)^2}{2(1.44)}}=0.3324\times0.9174=0.3050$；乘先驗 $\times0.4=0.1220$。
$0.1220 > 0.0105$ ⟹ 判給 $\omega_2$。與 $x=6.0$ 的結果相反——因為 $7.0$ 已越過門檻 $x^{*}=6.09$。
$p(7.0\mid\omega_1)=0.3989\,e^{-\frac{(2.5)^2}{2}}=0.0175$, times the prior $\times0.6=0.0105$. $p(7.0\mid\omega_2)=0.3324\,e^{-\frac{(0.5)^2}{2(1.44)}}=0.3050$, times the prior $\times0.4=0.1220$. $0.1220>0.0105 \Rightarrow$ classify as $\omega_2$ — the opposite of the $x=6.0$ result, because $7.0$ has crossed the threshold $x^{*}=6.09$.
2
概念理解 | Conceptual Understanding
「概似高」但「後驗低」是可能的嗎？請用 $x=6.0$ 的數字說明。
Is it possible to have "high likelihood" but "low posterior"? Explain using the numbers for $x=6.0$.
✅ 正確答案：
可能，而且正是 $x=6.0$ 的情況：$p(x\mid\omega_2)=0.1522 > p(x\mid\omega_1)=0.1295$，但乘上先驗後 $\omega_1$ 勝出。 概似只回答「這一類會不會長成這樣」，後驗還要考慮「這一類本來有多常見」。 醫學上的罕見病誤判，就是忘了乘先驗的經典後果。
Yes — that's exactly the $x=6.0$ case: $p(x\mid\omega_2)=0.1522 > p(x\mid\omega_1)=0.1295$, yet after multiplying by the prior, $\omega_1$ wins. Likelihood only answers "would this class look like this," while the posterior also weighs "how common is this class to begin with." Misdiagnosing rare diseases in medicine is the classic result of forgetting to multiply by the prior.
3
舉一反三 | Generalizing the Idea
圖 2 中「保留 96.7% 的變異」是什麼意思？如果只保留 40% 會發生什麼事？
What does "retaining 96.7% of the variance" mean in Fig. 2? What happens if only 40% is retained?
✅ 正確答案：
「變異」衡量資料的散開程度；保留 96.7% 表示投影後的一維座標，仍解釋了原本資料 96.7% 的散布， 只犧牲 3.3%——所以壓縮幾乎沒有損失。 若只保留 40%，代表你丟掉的方向仍帶有大量資訊，原本可分開的兩類很可能在投影後疊在一起，分類效能大幅下降。 這正是 §6 要討論「該保留幾維」的原因。
"Variance" measures how spread out the data is; keeping 96.7% means the projected one-dimensional coordinate still explains 96.7% of the original spread, sacrificing only 3.3% — so the compression is nearly lossless. Keeping only 40% means the discarded direction still carries a lot of information, and two originally separable classes will likely overlap after projection, sharply degrading classification performance. This is exactly why §6 discusses "how many dimensions to keep."

總結回顧 | Summary

線性代數告訴你「東西在哪」， 機率統計告訴你「你有多少把握」， Python 讓你能親眼確認前兩者沒有騙你。
Linear algebra tells you where things are; probability and statistics tell you how confident you are; Python lets you see with your own eyes that neither of them lied to you.

最怕的不是不會，是不知道自己不會。
The scariest thing isn't not knowing — it's not knowing that you don't know.
